# hotl

> hotl is a human-on-the-loop terminal AI agent in one static binary — no Node, no Python, no daemon, no telemetry. Bare `hotl` is the agent (full-screen console TUI, `-p "<prompt>"` headless, `--json` for a JSONL event stream, `--plan` for plan mode). `hotl watch` is a tmux dashboard for supervising agent processes. `hotl bg`/`hotl attach` run a session detached from any terminal. `hotl acp` serves ACP over stdio so an ACP-speaking editor can embed the agent. `hotl update` installs the latest release (`--check` only looks). `hotl fleet` is reserved and exits 2. Version 0.8.0; pre-1.0, breaking changes at every 0.x minor.

Facts an agent needs before acting:

- **Model selection:** `HOTL_MODEL=provider/model` env var (or `[provider].model` in config). Providers: `anthropic/…` (Messages API, needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and `openai/…` (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, LiteLLM — needs `OPENAI_API_KEY`; override the base URL with `HOTL_OPENAI_BASE_URL`). Keys never live in config.toml: use env vars, or `api_key_helper` (a command whose trimmed stdout is the key; 5s timeout, 64KB cap) — the helper beats static key env vars. For scalar settings, precedence is env var > config.toml > default.
- **Permission modes:** `bypass` (default — ordinary tool calls run without prompting) | `ask` (approve every mutating/executing call) | `dontask` (never wait for input; deny anything not pre-approved — the CI posture). Set via `HOTL_PERMISSIONS` or `[permissions] mode`. An unknown value fails closed to `ask`; `auto` is the old name for `bypass` and still parses. **Plan mode** is a separate axis, not a mode: `/plan`, `--plan`, `HOTL_PLAN=1`, or `[permissions] plan = true` makes `write`/`edit` always ask (never auto, not even via an allow-rule) while `bash`, MCP, and the web tools still follow the mode. It is a posture, not a mutation boundary — a shell redirect routes around it. Writes to protected paths (git hooks, shell rc, Makefiles, `.ssh/`, credential stores, agent-instruction files) always prompt, in every mode, and are checked before allow-rules. A `--features security-enforced` build ignores the mode key entirely.
- **Sandbox floor:** `bash` (and hooks and diagnostics) run confined by the kernel — Seatbelt on macOS, Landlock on Linux ≥ 6.2 including WSL2 — with writes limited to the working directory, the temp dir, `/dev`, and any extra directories in `[sandbox].writable` (out-of-workspace caches like bazel's; missing dirs are created at startup; entries exposing hotl's own config/data dirs are refused, so `~` and `/` can never be listed; `[sandbox].file_tools = "writable"` additionally opts the `write`/`edit` tools into those directories — default `"workspace"` keeps them workspace-only). Reads stay open. `HOTL_SANDBOX=off` disables it loudly. Windows native is unsupported; WSL2 is the Windows path. `Enforced` is proven at startup by a sandboxed child that must fail to write outside the confinement — not inferred from the mechanism being installed. Kernels 5.13–6.1 lack the Landlock truncate right and are not certified; `HOTL_SANDBOX=best-effort` accepts that partial floor, labeled `sandboxed:landlock(partial)`. Provider credentials are stripped from every child environment. On macOS the container-daemon socket class and Apple Events are denied by default (`HOTL_UNIX_SOCKETS=open`, `HOTL_MACOS_AUTOMATION=allow` opt out, both labeled in the ask). Where the floor cannot be enforced hotl degrades **fail-closed**: every exec is individually human-gated with an `UNSANDBOXED` banner and bash allow-rules stop applying. This is write-confinement, not exfiltration prevention.
- **Network egress:** `[network] egress` is `open` (default) | `off` (loopback and unix sockets only) | `allowlist` (loopback plus `[network].allow` hosts, `*.domain` wildcards matching apex and any depth, case-insensitive, no ports; an empty list allows nothing). Allowed hosts are reached through a small local proxy; tools that ignore proxy env vars do not get around it — they hit the kernel's loopback-only wall and fail. An unknown value fails closed to `off`. `web_fetch`/`web_search` honor the same single authority — there is no second allowlist. Limits: only HTTP traverses the proxy (SSH git remotes fail while restricted), an allowed host is allowed for *everything*, and DNS still resolves — a brake on casual exfiltration, not a cleanroom. On Linux this confines TCP only and needs kernel ≥ 6.7; where it cannot be enforced every bash ask shows `NET:UNENFORCED(reason)` and bash allow-rules stop auto-approving. Active state appears in each bash ask as `net:off` / `net:allow(N)`.
- **Context handling:** tool results larger than `[context].evict_tokens` (default 20000; `0` disables) are evicted to files — a preview stays inline and the agent pages the full result back on demand. Compaction summaries are precomputed in the background from ~60% context-full and fold in at ~80%, appending to history rather than replacing it, so the fold never pauses the session and a failed compaction cannot corrupt a session. The prompt prefix is byte-stable to keep provider prompt caches hot.
- **Engine defaults** (not yet env-configurable): max 25 turns per prompt, 32000 max output tokens, adaptive thinking on, static prompt caching on, and a tool that fails 5 times consecutively stops the turn.
- **State:** config in `~/.config/hotl/config.toml` (the only settings file — permissions, MCP, hooks, retrieval are all sections in it); append-only session logs in `~/.local/share/hotl/sessions/<ulid>.jsonl`; per-session git snapshots in `~/.local/share/hotl/shadow/<ulid>.git`. `hotl resume` continues a session, `hotl undo` reverses the agent's file edits, `hotl gc [--dry-run] [--days N] [--keep N]` prunes per `[retention]`. Secret-named env values are masked at log write time, and secret-bearing files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_*`, `.ssh/`, `.aws/`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.netrc`, `secrets.*`, `credentials`) are excluded from the snapshot store. Session logs are otherwise sensitive and permanent by design — there is no automatic cleanup of shadow snapshots yet.
- **Untrusted content:** everything returned by a sub-agent, `recall`, `web_fetch`/`web_search`, or an MCP tool arrives inside a provenance-tagged envelope — data that can inform the work, never an instruction the model may act on unprompted.
- **Extension points:** stdio MCP servers (`[[mcp]]`, inspected with `hotl mcp list|show|add|untrust|test` — read-mostly: it never writes `config.toml` and has no verb that grants trust, since trust is recorded only by a human answering the in-session fingerprint screen; `untrust` is its one mutation); `[[retrieval]]` backends behind one `recall` tool (nothing configured by default); `spawn` sub-agents with built-in (`general-purpose`, `explore`, `plan`) or user `agents/*.md` types; `skills/*.md` procedures plus `hotl skills` marketplaces — indexed, never preloaded: a grouped index is all that rides in context, and a skill's text loads only when the agent loads it; six hook events (`pre_tool`, `post_tool`, `user_prompt`, `notification`, `stop`, `session_end`) that can block or add context but never grant; `[diagnostics]` commands that run after edits. Claude Code's `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.claude/agents`, and plugin layouts load in place, no porting.
- **Setup check:** `hotl doctor` prints ok/FAIL lines for provider/keys, sandbox, config, allow-rules, session store, memory, secrets audit, and undo/git. Exit code is nonzero on failure. `hotl setup` writes a commented starter config.
- **Exit codes:** `0` turn completed; `130` interrupted; `1` any other outcome (error, refusal, turn-limit, doom-loop, tool-failure budget, or a `doctor` FAIL); `2` bad usage or a reserved subcommand (`fleet`).

## Docs

- [Overview](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/overview/): design commitments — session log, permission gate, provider seams, protocols, surfaces
- [Quickstart](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/quickstart/): install through first approved edit and undo, with expected output per step
- [Configuration](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/configuration/): every subcommand, config key, env var, and exit code
- [Permissions & sandbox](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/permissions-and-sandbox/): what the gate and sandbox protect and what they deliberately do not
- [Troubleshooting](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/troubleshooting/): error message → cause → fix table
- [TUI console](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/tui/): interactive console keys, opt-in vim input mode (`[behavior] vim_mode`, default off), prompt history and Ctrl-R search
- [Shell integration](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/shell/): zsh `: ` prefix, `@[path]` file capture, OSC-133 marks
- [Background sessions](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/backgrounding/): `hotl bg` / `hotl attach` detached sessions, with asks parked until you reattach
- [Skills](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/skills/): saved procedures loaded on demand — the grouped index, search, why there is no index database, trust envelope, marketplaces
- [Sub-agents](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/agents/): `spawn`, built-in agent types, `agents/*.md` definitions, `fork`
- [Retrieval (recall)](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/retrieval/): plugging a search backend in behind the `recall` tool
- [MCP servers](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/mcp/): connecting stdio MCP tool servers
- [Hooks & diagnostics](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/hooks/): post-edit diagnostics and the six hook events
- [Gateways](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/gateway/): OpenAI-compatible gateways and command-sourced API keys
- [Uninstall](https://nrakochy.github.io/hotl/uninstall/): removal, including data locations

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/nrakochy/hotl): Rust workspace; `crates/hotl` is the binary, library crates carry no semver promise
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/nrakochy/hotl/blob/master/ARCHITECTURE.md): layers and event flow
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/nrakochy/hotl/blob/master/docs/SECURITY.md): the security stance, including what the sandbox does not cover
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/nrakochy/hotl/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md): release history; breaking changes land at every 0.x minor
